_: THE v1 -> v2 SUCCESSOR MAP. Every v1 document either names the (topology, quant) lane that replaces it, or is listed with the reason it has none. Silence is not allowed: the regression fails on a document that is in neither list.

no_successor.dit.blocks-fused-qkv@1: NOT A LANE, BY DESIGN — it was a FRAGMENT, and tensorfs#127 exists because v1 could not say so. In v2 a fragment is a morphism seam file, and only topologies can be named by a lanes= declaration.
no_successor.sdxl.clip-g-fused-qkv@1: NOT A LANE — the fused half of a packaging pair. Its content is now spec/v2/morphisms/sdxl.clip-g-split-to-fused.v1.json, ratified evidence and all.
no_successor.sdxl.clip-g-split-qkv@1: NOT A LANE — the split half of the same pair, same seam file.
no_successor.flux1.diffusers-bf16@1: REFERENCE UNREACHABLE: black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev answers HTTP 401 to an anonymous header range. A topology is extracted from a reference tree, so an ungated read is the prerequisite; add the SOURCES.tsv line and rebuild.
no_successor.krea-2.diffusers-bf16@1: REFERENCE GATED: krea/Krea-2-Raw needs HF_TOKEN. Same prerequisite as flux1.
no_successor.internvl-u.diffusers-bf16@1: NOT YET EXTRACTED: reachable, but not banked in this change. One SOURCES.tsv line plus a rebuild.
no_successor.trellis2.dit-bf16@1: NOT YET EXTRACTED: the reference is assembled from several upstream repos, so it needs a composed SOURCES entry rather than one line.
no_successor.rife.flownet-fp32@1: NO UPSTREAM HEADER TO EXTRACT FROM. tensorhub/rife-4.25 is PRODUCED pod-side from an upstream pickle; the banked inventory (scripts/rife-4.25-inventory.json) carries name/dtype/rank and no SHAPES, which is exactly what a v2 topology is. Re-derive it from the producing module's state_dict with shapes, then extract.
no_successor.qwen3.6-27b-mtp.gguf-ud-q4-k-xl@1: GGUF: needs a gguf quant rule, which this change did not write. The topology extractor already reads GGUF headers (bank-headers.py does), so the missing half is the rule.
no_successor.qwen3.6-35b-a3b.vllm-fp8@1: MEASURED MISMATCH, not an oversight: the fp8 release carries 64196 tensors across 42 members and the bf16 release 1045 across 26 — the fp8 packaging also splits the MoE experts, so it is a DIFFERENT topology, needing its own extraction and a vllm rule. See spec/v2/baselines/stamps.json.

intentional_diffs.why: v2 GAINED A CAPABILITY v1 DID NOT HAVE. v1 could only compare a checkpoint to one document and had no way to say that two packagings are the same network, so it refused. v2 relates them through a ratified morphism and answers with the job that closes the gap. This is the direction the design calls for: over-constraint is the failure tensorfs#122's matching-set ruling forbids.

v1 FALSE CONVERSION OFFER. v1 reached a dtype disagreement before any structural one and reported `derivable`, so the gate would have enqueued and PAID FOR a cast job whose output still could not serve `ernie.diffusers-bf16@1` — `sd-turbo` is a different model. v1 REFUSED ITS OWN REFERENCE. `z-image.diffusers-bf16@1` declared BF16 for keys the shipped `z-image` tree carries at F32, so v1 offered a cast for the very checkpoint the document was derived from. v2's plain rules are reference-tolerant on islands — a key the reference itself ships at a wider compute type is accepted at either — so the reference admits, and no pointless conversion is billed.

_diff_summary.note: Every divergence from the v1 baseline is v1 being wrong in a direction the design named: false admits, conversion jobs offered for checkpoints no conversion could make servable, refusals v2 turns into ratified derivations, and one reference checkpoint v1 refused for carrying an F32 island. The four sdxl-inpainting-bf16 rows are THE HOLE: v1's own engine SATISFIES a 9-channel conv_in against the 4-channel SDXL lane, on all 1680 tensors.
